new_statements.quote: Sur ce gabarit restreint se joue un eventail d'articulations secondaires : toutes les varietes ont entre trois et cinq tons basiques avec des tons melodiques, la nasalisation et la phonation non-modale. [...] CVh est note en I-Sochiapan et Lalana, Lacova, Petlapa, Teotalcingo, Rio Chiquito, et La Alicia, une serie de localites de la variete IV, les memes localites ayant la balisticite. En suivant l'analyse de Herrera (2000), la frication glottale finale n'est autre que la balisticite ce qui permet de la traiter non comme un segment plein mais comme une realisation de ce contraste au niveau syllabique, la balisticite. [fn. 8:] Pour rappel : Usila et Sochiapan (variete I) ; Palantla et Tepetotutla (variete II), toutes les localites de la variete IV ; et Quiotepec et Comaltepec (variete V).
new_statements.translation: On this restricted template a range of secondary articulations is played out: all the varieties have between three and five basic tones with contour tones, nasalisation and non-modal phonation. [...] CVh is noted in I-Sochiapan and Lalana, Lacova, Petlapa, Teotalcingo, Rio Chiquito and La Alicia, a series of variety-IV localities, the same localities that have ballisticity. Following Herrera (2000), final glottal frication is nothing other than ballisticity, which allows it to be treated not as a full segment but as a realisation of this syllable-level contrast, ballisticity. [fn. 8:] As a reminder [localities with ballisticity]: Usila and Sochiapan (variety I); Palantla and Tepetotutla (variety II), all the localities of variety IV; and Quiotepec and Comaltepec (variety V).

new_statements.relation_note: Family/diasystem-level: 3-5 basic tones in all varieties; ballisticity (a laryngeal syllable-level contrast 'lie a l'accent') attested in all variety-IV localities incl. Petlapa and Teotalcingo; discusses Mugele 1984 on Lalana ballistic stress.
new_statements.rule_in_words: All Chinantec dialect groups, including variety IV to which Petlapa and Teotalcingo (Tepinapa-area) belong, are tonal with three to five level tones plus contours; Petlapa and Teotalcingo forms in Rensch's data show CVh, read as ballistic (vs controlled) syllables. Nothing on the position of word stress.
new_statements.exceptions: fn. 4: tones for Tepetotutla, Ozumacin, Villa Nacional, Latani, Lealao and Yolox are not given in Rensch 1968 (Petlapa/Teotalcingo not in that list, but Rensch 1968 sec. 1.14 itself says no tone analysis was available for them -- unresolved); author warns the age/nature of the data do not permit fine-grained phonetic analysis and that the ballisticity list is 'provisoire'.
new_statements.identity_note: Diasystemic (structural-dialectology) re-analysis of Rensch 1968's 194-cognate x 23-locality data (MAmP digital corpus); Petlapa and Teotalcingo (Tepinapa-area / 'sureste medio' towns, see works[0]) are among the 18 second-tier localities and are placed in 'variete IV, basses terres meridionales' with Lalana, Lealao, Latani, Lacova, Rio Chiquito, La Alicia. Statements about Petlapa/Teotalcingo are second-hand readings of Rensch's notation, not new fieldwork.

new_statements.relation_note: First-hand tone system of a cte variety (9 tones, 5 levels, 28 tone x syllable-type patterns, tonal processes, regular tone correspondences with Lalana, Ozumacin, Comaltepec in B.2.3-B.4); tonic/pretonic organisation with root-final stress marks; explicit statement that Jocotepec and Petlapa tone systems diverge from Lalana's.
new_statements.rule_in_words: TONE (first-hand, cte locality Arroyo Blanco Petlapa): nine contrastive tones on the tonic syllable -- five levels /1 2 3 4 5/ (1 = lowest) plus contours /23 24 32 42/ -- cross-classified with five syllable types (long/short vowel x modal, final or medial glottalization), 28 attested patterns (Cuadro B.1); tone /4/ with modal voice possibly only derived; a floating /(5)/, /24/-splitting and /5/-/5/ downstep-type dissimilation operate rightwards across syllables (B.2.2). Stress: the description is organised around a tonic syllable vs pretonic syllables (pretonic syllables carry only /1 2 3 4 5 24/); every cited form carries the stress mark on the root = last syllable of the prosodic word, enclitics excluded (e.g. ɕi²ˈʔjaː⁴ 'abuela', ri³ˈkʷo³na³ 'lo permitiremos'); the explicit rule -- stress demarcative, on the final syllable of the prosodic word (= last/only root syllable), not lexically contrastive, loans may be penultimate/antepenultimate -- is stated for Lalana in sec. 2.4.1 and carried over terminologically, not restated, for Petlapa. Nakamoto treats final aspiration as a phonetic property of certain tones, not as 'ballistic stress' (sec. 3.1, p. 78, for Lalana; tones /32 42 3/ described with 'aspiracion final' in Cuadro B.1 for Petlapa).
new_statements.secondary_stress: none described; pretonic syllables (prefixes, non-final root syllables, first members of compounds) are unstressed with a reduced tone inventory.
new_statements.exceptions: For Lalana (sec. 2.4.1/2.5.1): Spanish loans may keep penultimate or antepenultimate stress; enclitics fall outside the prosodic word and are unstressed. For Petlapa: tone /4/ with modal voice may be marginal/derived only; distribution of coda /n/ 'mas restringida' and not yet worked out; the author calls the appendix 'apuntes' based on c. 2,000 elicited items.
new_statements.identity_note: PASS-1 WORK (our_bibliography: 'Nakamoto 2026.. not located', access unknown, unread), added: (1) an OPEN copy (TESIUNAM, deposited Jan-Mar 2026), downloaded, saved to the mirror and read; (2) a first-hand TONE statement for a Tepinapa-Chinantec [cte] locality that no earlier reading had: Appendix B.2 describes the variety of Santa Cecilia Arroyo Blanco, agencia of San Juan Petlapa municipality, from c. 2,000 words/phrases elicited 2024- with speaker Elias Ojeda Toledo. Identity: INALI's catalogue lists 'Arroyo Blanco' and 'San Juan Petlapa' under jujmi <chinanteco del sureste medio>, the INALI variant that ELCat/Glottolog equate with cte (tepi1241); Ethnologue places cte in San Juan Petlapa and Santiago Jocotepec municipalities; Nakamoto (p. 509-510) says Petlapa town, San Felipe el Mirador and Arroyo Blanco speak 'una variedad casi identica' while Lovani, Toavela and Santa Isabel Cajonos (the other cte towns) speak 'variedades distintas', and (p. 7, sec. 1.2) he deliberately excludes Jocotepec and Petlapa from 'chinanteco de Lalana' because 'el sistema tonal de Jocotepec (notas de campo) y el de Petlapa (B.2) son suficientemente divergentes, y una buena parte de la descripcion tonal para Lalana no es valida para Jocotepec o Petlapa' -- i.e. this is NOT a Lalana (lala1270) statement applied by proxy but a separate description of a cte variety inside a Lalana grammar. He also states (p. 27, 510) that the variety 'no cuenta con estudios previos, mas que los datos lexicos esporadicos sin notacion tonal en Rensch (1989)'. The body of the grammar (chs. 2-3: Lalana segmental phonology, 13 tones with underspecification, demarcative word-final stress) is lala1270.

The 9 tones cross-classify with 5 syllable types by vowel length and phonation /Vː VˀV Vːˀ V Vˀ/ (coda /n/ adds a mora), giving 28 attested patterns (Cuadro B.1, p. 512, with examples); level /4/ with modal voice may be marginal, arising only from tonal processes.
